title: Priority Banding & GPU-fit Proposal for Enterprise Dedicated Requests
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Create a repeatable intake + triage workflow that maps enterprise dedicated capacity requests to priority bands, SLA targets, reserved throughput profiles, GPU class recommendations, and scaling policy templates. Deliver a lightweight rubric and intake form that enables sales/solutions to scope asks consistently and a decision matrix for fast approvals.
problem_statement: Currently enterprise reserved requests are triaged ad-hoc: SLA expectations, GPU class, and scaling policies are estimated inconsistently across reps and SEs. This causes long negotiation cycles, overprovisioning, and delivery surprises when workloads hit production. We need a deterministic process that balances customer needs, cost, and platform constraints.
goals: Reduce average time-to-decision for dedicated capacity requests from 10 business days to <= 3 business days
Standardize SLA definitions and mapping to reserved throughput and GPU class
Provide guardrails that limit unreasonable overprovisioning while keeping predictable application behavior
Produce artifacts: intake form, triage rubric, decision matrix, and sample customer letters for SLA exceptions
success_metrics: Decision time <= 3 business days for 90% of requests
<10% of onboarding customers requiring post-commit SLA rework in first 30 days
Average committed GPU hours saved vs current baseline (target 15% reduction)
Time to first meaningful throughput in production <= 5 business days after capacity commit
scope_in_scope: Design intake form fields for sales/SEs
Define 3 priority bands with explicit SLA/throughput/GPU mappings (Band 1/2/3)
Map common model families to GPU class recommendations (A100, H100, L4x etc) and quantized variants
Create suggested autoscaling policy templates and preemption rules
Deliver triage rubric and approval workflow for PM, Infra, and Solutions
scope_out_of_scope: Billing contract language updates (legal to handle separately)
Implementation of new autoscaler in runtime (engineering follow-up tickets)
proposed_design: Introduce a three-band priority model: Band Alpha (mission-critical, SLO 99.95, p95 latency target per model defined, reserved baseline + hot burst pool, H100 preferred), Band Beta (business-critical, SLO 99.5, higher latency tolerance, A100/L4x depending on cost/throughput), Band Gamma (best-effort reserved, SLO 99.0, optimized for cost with lower GPU class and stronger burst throttling). Each band includes: a) reserved baseline throughput (tokens/sec or qps), b) burst budget (credits) and preemption policy, c) KV cache targets and batching knobs, d) fallback chains of compatible model variants for graceful degradation. Intake form will compute a suggested band and GPU mapping based on workload fingerprint (token lengths, concurrency, expected p95 latency requirement, peak qps), and surface cost tradeoffs to the customer.
